legal_name: iMENA Holding (Saudi closed joint stock company), trading as iMENA Group
variant_flag: A holding company whose platforms sell to consumers and also to car dealers and merchants. Chose B2C because its value sits in consumer platforms with more than 100 million users.
target_audience: Your target customers are people across Saudi Arabia and the wider Middle East and North Africa who buy and sell cars and goods online and book rides by app, and you reach them through OpenSooq, SellAnyCar and Jeeny. Online marketplace and app brands are already in the sport to reach the same kind of user: Mercado Libre (Alpine), Airtasker (Racing Bulls), viagogo (Alpine) and Skip (Alpine).
market_overlap: iMENA is headquartered in Riyadh, and its platforms serve more than 100 million users in over 20 countries across the Middle East and North Africa. The Formula 1 calendar aligns with the markets you are present in and expanding into: Jeddah, Bahrain, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.
market_reference: Mercado Libre, your closest peer as a regional online marketplace leader, has partnered with Alpine since 2025 and renewed for 2026. Its logo runs on the car all season, and it builds campaigns around driver Franco Colapinto to reach fans across Latin America, its home region.
shared_values: A Formula 1 team is made of specialist departments that share data and tools to move faster together. iMENA is building its group the same way, with its platforms set to share technology, data and operations.
f1_audience: Formula 1 has 827M fans, up 12% in a year, and 43% are under 35. Against a general population index of 100, fans score 126 for researching online before buying and 200 for brand loyalty. The sport reached a total audience of 1.83bn in 2025.
flags: Capacity: soft note. Completed a SAR 802M (USD 214M) capital increase in two tranches, announced 16 Nov 2026, after a USD 135M pre-IPO round in April 2025. The 2025 round was described as private placement plus in-kind contributions, so not all of it is cash. Revenue, valuation and the investors in the latest tranche are not disclosed; Al Rajhi Capital advised.

State-linked shareholder: Sanabil Investments, an investment arm of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, backed the 2025 round and is in the investor base with other Saudi institutions. Not majority state-owned on the facts found. Mission-level language only; no sanctions issue found in the sources opened.

Identity: built iMENA Group (iMENA Holding, imena.com), the Riyadh technology group co-founded in 2012 by Nasir Alsharif, Khaldoon Tabaza and Adey Salamin; CEO Sara Al-AlShaikh (in the role since April 2026). No other company of this name found.

Portfolio: the November 2026 release names OpenSooq (classifieds), SellAnyCar (car trading) and Jeeny (ride-hailing) as its platforms, but imena.com tags every portfolio card, including these three, Telr, HelloFood and JRD, as 'exited'. Confirm which platforms iMENA still controls, and whether the pitch should go to the group or to OpenSooq.

Calendar: Saudi Arabia is the home market (Jeddah). Bahrain, Qatar and Abu Dhabi are listed because the platforms cover over 20 countries in the region, and Telr serves UAE merchants; presence in Bahrain and Qatar was not confirmed country by country today.

Market reference is a peer in another region, not a competitor: Mercado Libre (Alpine) verified on alpinef1.com (renewal before the 2026 Australian Grand Prix, logo on the A526, Colapinto campaign). Reports in February 2026 said its logo had briefly left the car before the renewal.

Grid: Saudi-linked partners already in the sport include Aramco and Ma'aden (Aston Martin) and KAUST (McLaren). Rakuten joins Ferrari in 2027, so online marketplace is taken there; Mercado Libre holds e-commerce at Alpine.
IPO: the CEO calls a listing a natural option but gives no date; the 2025 round was described as the first pre-IPO tranche. Template note: fit_reason left empty under the 23 Nov 2026 template change.

priority.reason: Just completed a USD 214M capital increase, has a new chief executive and consumer platforms across a region with four races, and Mercado Libre at Alpine shows the model works for a regional marketplace.
